dossier.public_summary: The light curve shows two very different dip depths alternating every orbit with a second dip halfway around the orbit, classic for an eclipsing binary, not a planet. Depths swing from near zero to over 1600 ppm between sectors and between individual transits, driven by a few deep events that dominate the signal. Combined these prove the signal is an on-target binary/variability artifact, not a 1.7 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even dips differ at 10.87 sigma (depth_odd_ppm 850.3 vs depth_even_ppm 126.7, difference 723.6 ppm, ratio 6.7) – a textbook EB signature at twice the 13.1 d period, with 2 sectors >3 sigma and same-sign bias 0.6.
A secondary dip at phase 0.5537±0.0537 has SNR 7.85 depth_ppm 122.1 depth_over_dip 0.2937, exceeding best_brightening_snr 5.562, indicating stellar eclipse, not a planet.

Depth is not steady: SPOC 2-min depths range 51±95 ppm (sector 1) to 1689±128 ppm (sector 69) with chi2 188.3/7 dof and depth_change_pct 306.6, and transit_depths chi2 427.4350115356898/14 dof p_consistent 2.0781736921563344e-82.

The signal is dominated by 3 deep events (1798 ppm, 1652 ppm, 1399 ppm) and includes non-detections (-179 ppm, -187 ppm), consistent with a few bad/stochastic eclipses and strong red noise 1.542, not a stable planet.
Planet rank 0.12 is below 0.1 threshold typical for false positives, supporting the EB/variability interpretation over a planet.
